target.title: fix(signal): retry debounce flush on reply session initialization conflict
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal's debounce flush handler silently drops inbound messages when the reply session initialization throws a "reply session initialization conflicted" error. Slack and Telegram handlers already handle this error — Slack releases the seen message so it is re-polled, and Telegram applies a bounded retry. Signal has neither mechanism, so follow-up DMs sent shortly after a previous turn's reply are permanently lost with zero user-visible feedback.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof script (7/7 PASS)

```
node --import tsx test/_proof_signal_retry_conflict.mts

PASS  two conflicts then success: 3 total calls :: calls=3
PASS  always conflicts: error propagated :: err=Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:signal:direct:proof
PASS  always conflicts: 4 total calls (1 initial + 3 retries) :: calls=4
PASS  non-conflict error: propagated :: err=Error: some unrelated error
PASS  non-conflict error: only 1 call (no retry) :: calls=1
PASS  success on first attempt: only 1 call :: calls=1
PASS  custom params (2 retries, 50ms): 3 total calls :: calls=3

[proof] 7 PASS, 0 FAIL
```

The proof script calls the actual exported `dispatchWithRetryOnConflict` function (not a mock) and verifies: retry on conflict errors (3 total calls with backoff), error propagation after exhaustion, no retry on unrelated errors, and custom retry parameters honored.

### Why This Change Was Made

Because Signal receives messages via webhook/API rather than polling, the "release and re-poll" pattern used by Slack does not apply. Instead, the dispatch is wrapped with a bounded exponential backoff retry via the exported helper `dispatchWithRetryOnConflict`:

- Up to 3 retries (4 total attempts)
- Delays: 200ms → 400ms → 800ms
- Only retries on "reply session initialization conflicted" errors
- All other errors propagate to `onError` exactly as before

### Testing

- `test/_proof_signal_retry_conflict.mts` — real behavior proof (7 scenarios)
- Existing Signal event handler tests cover the debounce flush path

## Issue

Fixes #100944
